given: An acceptance criterion is declared optional, the file it looks for never appears, so the criterion is skipped on every run; the report records the skip but does not register it as 'skipped:<id>: <reason>' in known_limitations.
when: The verdict gate reads the report of that run.

expected.side_effects: the gate names the skip and the registration it expected, so the untraced skip cannot pass as a verdict=pass report

trigger.sandbox: the shape is built under the system temp directory by tests/gate-cases.Tests.ps1; the report is produced by tools\verify\run-test-report.ps1, then the registration line is removed from a copy of it
trigger.counterpart: the untouched report of the same run must pass: a traced skip is registered as 'skipped:<id>: <reason>' in known_limitations

why: Optionality does not turn 'not done' into 'did not need to be done'. A skip that never reaches the summary is the silent gap that optional checks used to create, and a run that claims success while asserting nothing is the failure this case exists to catch.
